Strawberries are easy as fuck. They can produce berries in their first year, but expect better fruits year 2+. I would water then daily for the first few days, then every other day until they're adapted to the local conditions. I have found strawberries don't need much care over all. Blackberries will need no help. They can take over your yard if you're not diligent.

If you haven't already used the sulphur, hold off. Sulphur increases acidity. Great for berry plants, but they may not require it if your soil is already a good acidity level (many local extension offices can do soil tests). I have personally never tested my soil, and my plants do well enough.

And I don't know what happy frog soil is, but you paid way too much.

"Happy Frog" is really meant for overly pretentious Weed Growers... If you wanted to grow anything regularly learn to appreciate composting, whether it's standard composting, vermiculture, whatever... You could even get a 50-55 gallon plastic drum and turn it into a quick composter a lot cheaper than you can buy a pre-fab one. Around here a lot of the smaller scale people, gardeners, etc. like to use Mushroom Compost, it's literally the stuff they use to grow commercial mushrooms in, because mushrooms are so different from plants the former grow medium for mushrooms, when spent for that purpose, is excellent for almost any plant, and a lot of local Feed & Seed stores sell it by the "scoop" or "bucket" which 2 scoops would fill up the back of a small truck... Oh and the "Scoop" {literally a tractor scoop} of Mushroom Compost was going for around $20 around here last time I bought 1, like I said though 2 scoops will load a small truck like and S-10 though, so loaded you won't want to try too many hills with it that loaded. You can also pay way too much for that in bags in most places carrying garden supplies, but it's generally not as fresh. Plus there's like a $5 bag versus 15 bags in a scoop for $20 maybe $25 at this point......
